This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 20.06.2023 at about 5.35 p.m, the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-Q-2466 from Yelahanka towards Hebbala in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached B.B.Road Hebbal Fly over Upramp, Hebbala, Bengaluru City, at that time suddenly the driver of Mahindra XUV car bearing Reg.No.KA- 51-MC-3254 moving towards Hebbala Fly over and moving left side and immediately he took his vehicle to right side without giving any signal in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life and dashed against to the petitioner's motorcycle and Karthik Gowda G vs Sunanda Devi C V on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170865830/

sentences.text: As a result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone several surgeries and was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
SCCH-23
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of driver of Mahindra XUV car.

The respondent No.1 being the owner of the car and she is liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through her counsel.
Statutory time for filing written statement has been elapsed.
Hence written statement taken as not filed.
4. The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to P13 were marked on his behalf.
Further Dr. Shashikanth was examined as PW.2 & through him Ex.P.14 to 18 were marked.
5. Arguments were addressed by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
In spite sufficient opportunity has been given, the respondent has not contested and also not addressed their arguments.
Hence arguments of respondent is SCCH-23 taken as nil.
However, liberty has to be given to file written arguments before two days from the date of pronouncement of judgment, they have not filed any written arguments.
Hence arguments of respondents side taken as nil.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

6. The following points are raised for consideration :
POINTS 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.06.2023 at about 5.35 p.m., B.B.Road Hebbal Fly over Upramp,
Hebbala, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Mahindra XUV car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-3254 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
7.

My answers to the above points are as follows :-

sentences.text: . POINT NO.1:

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver SCCH-23 of Mahindra XUV car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-3254 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 338 of IPC and u/s 146, 196 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
In spite of due service of the notice of petition upon her, the respondent appeared through her counsel.
Statutory time for filing written statement has been elapsed.
Hence written statement taken as not filed.

Added more Ex.P.8 being the statement of accused and owner and Ex.P.9 being order sheet in CC.No.3292/2023 discloses that the accused and owner of the car have pleaded guilty in the criminal case and paid the fine.
Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending vehicle is caused accident and in the accident the petitioner sustained injury.
Thus the evidence led by the petitioner has remained unchallenged.

Consequently, based on the material available on record, I hold that actionable negligence on the part of the driver of Mahindra XUV car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MC-3254 in causing the accident in question is proved.
Therefore, I answer point No.1 as 'In the Affirmative.
SCCH-23 9. POINT NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
10. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
So far as the age of the petitioner is concerned, he has not produced any documents to show his age.

The document available on record i.e., Aadhar card,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 21.07.1998.
This indicates that he was aged (24 years 10 months 30 days) 25 years on the date of accident.
The petitioner deposed that prior to the accident he was working as Therapy Manager, Entero Company and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of SCCH-23 Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.

Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the Karthik Gowda G vs Sunanda Devi C V on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170865830/

sentences.text: As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (1) Compound communited fracture of the left femur (thigh bone) (2) Undisplaced fracture of left knee, tibial spine.
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary of Manipal SCCH-23 Hospital (Ex.P.12) indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 20.06.2023 to 22.06.2023 (3 days in total).

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : Correction deformity done on 21.06.2025, wound debridement (debidement of gustilo type 3 (including subtypes) compound injuries or EQU done on 21.06.2025.
12.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Shashikanth as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 37% to the left leg and 12.33% disability to the whole body.
The PW.2 has not been cross examined by the respondent.
When such is the case physical disability assessed by the medical expert is on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment SCCH-23 of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctors, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 12%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 12%.
13.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 3 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.4,500/- (1,500 X 3) is awarded under this head.
14. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and SCCH-23 mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

15. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.64,000/- (16,000 X 4) under this head.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
As per the medical bills (13) marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner has spent Rs.3,38,699/- towards medical expenses.
The PW.1 has not been cross examined by the respondent.

On perusal of Sl.No.3 & 4 and Sl.No.7 & 8 are one and the same bills and the petitioner has Karthik Gowda G vs Sunanda Devi C V on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170865830/

sentences.text: Hence Sl.No.4 and 8 are not considered.
Further on perusal of Sl.No.13, the said bill is duplicate copy.
Further on going through the said bill wherein the Ins.Co.Name /TPA name is mentioned as Tata AIG Life Ins.Co.Ltd., Health India TPA services Pvt Ltd.

sentences.text: Further in SCCH-23 SL.No.13 at page No.10 it is mentioned the total bill amount is Rs.3,38,146/- and the hospital authority has been given discount of Rs.18,146/-, thereafter the net total amount comes to Rs.3,20,000/-.
Further the Health India TPA services paid his share for a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- and further it is mentioned the patient share for a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-.
The other bills have been meticulously examined and is found to be correct.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence after deduction of (Rs.2,923/-, Rs.514/- and Rs.2,00,000/-) the petitioner is entitled only a sum of Rs.1,35,262/- which is rounded off to Rs.1,35,300/- is awarded under this head.
17. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.4,14,720/- (Rs.16,000 X 12 X 18 X 12%) which is rounded off to Rs.4,14,700/- is awarded under this head.

SCCH-23 18. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under this head.
19. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The doctor witness has stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.80,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which he has to necessarily bear certain expenses.
Thus he is entitled to Rs.30,000/- towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

Medical expenses : 1,35,300-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 4,14,700-00 disability SCCH-23 6 Loss of future amenities & : 50,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : 30,000-00 Total 7,48,500-00 21.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: The respondent is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
She has not produced any document to show that her vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the driver of offending car, the respondent is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.
Hence he is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
SCCH-23 23. POINT NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,48,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH-23 Draw award accordingly.
